analyst.summary: Union Bank of India's asset quality keeps improving on the surface - gross NPAs down to 2.65% and net NPAs to 0.47% as of June 2026, with strong capital (18.46% CRAR) - and profitability metrics (17%+ ROE, 1.36% ROA) are good for a PSU bank. But a meaningful part of the recent profit jump comes from lower provisions rather than pure business improvement, deposits are growing much slower than loans, some early stress is showing up in small-business accounts, and a large capital raise is in the pipeline that will dilute existing shareholders. At roughly book value, the stock looks fairly priced for what it can sustainably deliver once these tailwinds fade - not expensive, but not offering a discount either. We rate it a Hold.
